taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, using only the rule descriptions provided.

## 1. Loop-drawing puzzles
These require drawing a single continuous loop.

- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop through cells; white circles must be handled uniformly by region; black circles are avoided.
- **Masyu** — loop through black and white circles; white circles force straight passage with a turn nearby, black circles force a turn with straight continuation.
- **Mid-loop** — single loop through cells; must pass through all black circles as midpoints of straight segments.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop; must visit each room only once and in each room use either all moon cells or all sun cells.
- **Nagareru** — single continuous loop with a consistent direction, following arrows and wind constraints.
- **Slitherlink** — loop on dot grid; numbers indicate how many surrounding lines each cell has.
- **Suraromu** — single loop through cells; must pass all gates and obey gate-order constraints from the numbered circle.
- **Yajilin** — single loop through cells; numbered arrows indicate black cells in a direction.
- **Kurodoko** is not a loop puzzle.
- **Numberlink** is a path puzzle, not a loop puzzle.

## 2. Path / connection puzzles
These involve connecting targets with lines or tracks, but not necessarily one global loop.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges.
- **Numberlink** — connect pairs of same numbers with continuous lines.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles through tracks so each country gets one circle.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas via arrows.
- **Pencils** — draw lines from pencil tips using pencil lengths.
- **Evolomino** — arrows define block progressions by adding one square.
- **Hebi** — snake numbers 1 to 5 must be sequentially connected.
- **Nagareru** — although loop-based, it is also a directed path problem.
- **Sashigane** — L-shaped blocks defined by arrows/open circles.
- **Nuritwin** — shaded cells must connect across regions.

## 3. Region partition / tiling puzzles
These require dividing the grid into regions or blocks with structural constraints.

- **Chained Block** — black-cell blocks must be formed into chains; no duplicate shape in a chain.
- **Choco Banana** — paint cells black so black regions are rectangles/squares, white regions are not.
- **Double Choco** — divide into blocks containing matching white/gray shapes.
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into blocks of five cells.
- **Fillomino** — divide into numbered blocks matching block sizes.
- **Heyawake** — rooms with painted-cell counts; white cells have line-span restrictions.
- **LITS** — fill each room with a tetromino; same-shaped tetrominoes may not touch edgewise.
- **Nurikabe** — white islands and one continuous black wall; no 2×2 black.
- **Nuritwin** — each region must contain exactly two same-sized shaded blocks.
- **Shikaku** — divide grid into rectangles, each containing one number matching area.
- **Sto-stone** — black cells within rooms, with gravity-like dropping behavior.
- **Sudoku** — fill cells under row/column/3×3 block constraints.
- **Ripple Effect** — rooms contain consecutive numbers starting from 1.
- **Juosan** — fill cells with horizontal or vertical marks inside territories.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers and obey arrow-max rules.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares.
- **Tilepaint** — tiles must be uniformly colored or uncolored; diagonal numbers constrain counts.

## 4. Coloring / shading puzzles
These are mainly about coloring cells black/white or equivalent marks.

- **Akari** — place light bulbs; illuminate white cells.
- **Hitori** — blacken cells so duplicates are removed and white cells remain connected.
- **Kurodoko** — color cells black so numbered cells see the correct number of white cells.
- **Kurotto** — color cells around circles according to black-cell sums.
- **Nurikabe** — shade cells black to form a continuous wall with isolated white islands.
- **Nurimeizu** — paint cells black to create a maze from S to G, with room-based constraints.
- **Nurimisaki** — decide white “Misaki” cells and black cells while keeping white cells connected.
- **Usowan** — color cells with exactly one wrong number per room.
- **Choco Banana** — black/white area structure with rectangle/square constraints.
- **Norinori** — place blocks in pairs in consecutive black squares.
- **Chained Block** — black-cell blocks and chain constraints.

## 5. Number-placement puzzles
These require placing numbers under rules.

- **Sudoku** — place 1–9 with row/column/block uniqueness.
- **Fillomino** — fill regions with numbers equal to region size.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers; room contents and arrow constraints.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1.
- **Nansuke** — fill blanks with numbers from a given list, respecting digit placement format.
- **Juosan** — fill with — or |, not numbers, so not in this category.
- **Usowan** — numbers are clues, but the task is coloring cells, not placing numbers.

## 6. Object/shape construction puzzles
These involve assembling a specified shape or shape family.

- **LITS** — tetrominoes in each room, avoiding same-shape edge contact.
- **Sashigane** — all blocks must be L-shaped.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles to shape remaining white regions.
- **Choco Banana** — blocks must be rectangles/squares.
- **Five Cells** — all blocks must have exactly five cells.
- **Double Choco** — paired shapes of white and gray areas.
- **Evolomino** — block shape grows by one square along an arrow route.
- **Pencils** — pencil shapes and lines from tips.
- **Hebi** — snake-shaped sequential number chains.

## 7. Constraint puzzles on visibility, distance, or line-of-sight
These depend on counting or seeing in a direction.

- **Akari** — bulbs illuminate along rows/columns until blocked.
- **Kurodoko** — numbers count visible white cells to nearest black/frame.
- **Kurotto** — circles sum consecutive black cells extending from them.
- **Hebi** — arrow-direction visibility determines numbers.
- **Makaro** — arrows point to the maximum adjacent number.
- **Ripple Effect** — duplicated numbers in row/column must be spaced apart.
- **Yajilin** — arrows count black cells in that direction.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move through cells until each country has one.
- **Yosenabe** — circles move into gray areas, arrows show movement.

## 8. Adjacency / non-adjacency puzzles
These rely heavily on whether regions or objects may touch.

- **Hitori** — black cells never touch; white cells must connect.
- **Nurikabe** — black wall must connect; no 2×2 black.
- **LITS** — same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch edgewise.
- **Nuritwin** — two blocks in a region must not touch edgewise.
- **Norinori** — blocks are placed in twos in consecutive black squares.
- **Shakashaka** — white leftover areas must be rectangles/squares.
- **Usowan** — colored cells cannot connect; white cells must stay connected.
- **Choco Banana** — black and white areas have distinct connectivity/shaping constraints.
- **Akari** — bulbs cannot illuminate each other.

## 9. Room-based puzzles
These explicitly use bold-line bounded rooms or territories.

- **Heyawake**
- **Juosan**
- **Makaro**
- **Moon-or-Sun**
- **Nurimeizu**
- **Nurimisaki**
- **Ripple Effect**
- **Shikaku**
- **Sto-stone**
- **Tilepaint**
- **Usowan**
- **Yosenabe**
- **Double Choco**
- **LITS**
- **Nurikabe**
- **Nuritwin**
- **Sashigane**
- **Suraromu**
- **Chained Block**
- **Choco Banana**
- **Five Cells**

## 10. Arrow / direction-based puzzles
These use arrows as core constraints.

- **Hebi** — arrows on black cells show viewed counts.
- **Makaro** — black arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Nagareru** — arrows define loop direction and wind direction.
- **Pencils** — pencil tips are marked by arrows/shapes; lines extend from tips.
- **Sashigane** — arrows point toward the knee of an L-shaped block.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move along tracks; arrows show movement in the sample visuals.
- **Suraromu** — gate ordering is tied to numbered start position.
- **Yajilin** — numbered arrows indicate black-cell counts in a direction.
- **Yosenabe** — arrows represent movement paths into gray areas.
- **Shakashaka** — not an arrow puzzle.

|---|---|
| Loop puzzles | Dotchi-Loop, Masyu, Mid-loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Slitherlink, Suraromu, Yajilin |
| Connection/path puzzles | Hashiwokakero, Numberlink, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Pencils, Hebi, Evolomino, Nagareru |
| Partition/tiling puzzles | Chained Block, Choco Banana, Double Choco, Five Cells, Fillomino, Heyawake, LITS, Nurikabe, Nuritwin, Shikaku, Sto-stone, Sudoku, Ripple Effect, Juosan, Makaro, Shakashaka, Tilepaint |
| Coloring/shading puzzles | Akari, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Nurikabe, Nurimeizu, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Norinori |
| Number-placement puzzles | Sudoku, Fillomino, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Nansuke |
| Shape-construction puzzles | LITS, Sashigane, Shakashaka, Choco Banana, Five Cells, Double Choco, Evolomino, Pencils, Hebi |
| Visibility/distance puzzles | Akari, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Hebi, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Yajilin, Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| Adjacency/non-adjacency puzzles | Hitori, Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin, Norinori, Usowan, Akari, Choco Banana |
